visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 more accurately visualizes the actual geometry with internally tangent nested circles sharing a common point and correctly shaded gap regions, whereas Lesson 2 mostly shows algebra without a positional circle diagram and therefore provides less direct visual confirmation of the shaded regions.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed quiz gate after act_total_area with a real question, plausible options, and a marked correct answer, while Lesson 2 has no gate specs or plan at all, so it provides no functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, paced narration with math spoken naturally, while Lesson 2 is a dense run-on transcript containing raw symbolic expressions like πx2k² and 2k-1² that would be read awkwardly or ambiguously by TTS.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 has explicit cues that generally occur near the narrated references, while Lesson 2 provides no beat or cue timing at all, so its many formula and testing references have no demonstrated synchronized visual changes.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 presents the ring-area difference and summation with correct, explicit algebra and clearer scaffolding from one shaded region to the inequality, while Lesson 2 reaches the right answer but its transcript contains ambiguous or incorrect algebraic wording such as the malformed square-difference expression before jumping to the correct simplification.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is more consistently composed without distracting playback UI overlays, while Lesson 2 has a cleaner mid-slide but suffers from excessive empty space, barely visible subtitle text, visible cursor/UI controls/captions, and a less polished title presentation.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents preferred Lesson 1. The strongest signals were interactivity, narration quality, and concept accuracy: Lesson 1 has a functioning quiz gate, clearer and more natural narration, and more accurate/scaffolded algebra. Visual accuracy also favored Lesson 1 because it actually depicts the nested tangent circles and shaded gap regions, while Lesson 2 relies mostly on algebra. Sync and polish were somewhat lower-confidence but still favored Lesson 1 due to explicit timing cues and fewer distracting presentation issues. With unanimous votes and several high-confidence judgments, Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner.
